name: Grave Candle
description: Summons a corpse-light that reveals recent death, burial disturbance, and lingering spirit presence.

name: Last Whisper
description: Draws a fading emotional or sensory residue from a recent death: fear, grief, duty, betrayal, direction, or final intent.

name: Gravechill
description: Drains warmth and vigor from a target, leaving limbs heavy and concentration brittle.

name: Bone Hand
description: Animates a small fragment of bone or dead matter into a pointer, dart, messenger, or simple manipulator.

name: Rest the Dead
description: Still a corpse, quiet a weak haunting, and prevent immediate rise, theft, or defilement of remains.

name: Speak with Remains
description: Questions a corpse, skull, ash, or relic for fragments of memory, identity, and knowledge.

name: Siphon Vigor
description: Transfers a sliver of life-force from one creature to steady, mend, or sustain another.

name: Tomb Ward
description: Sets funerary protection against spirit escape, corpse theft, hostile animation, and grave violation.

name: Raise Servitor
description: Animates one or more simple undead for labor, transport, watch duty, or basic combat obedience.

name: Chain a Ghost
description: Compels a spirit to remain, answer, guide, testify, or cease torment under enforced terms.

name: Black Harvest
description: Draws deeply on recent death or grave-force to fuel major necromantic workings at ethical or physical cost.

name: Legion Call
description: Raises and coordinates a disciplined cluster of dead into useful organized function.

name: Field of Ashen Silence
description: Attunes a broad area to death: vitality weakens, sound dulls, healing becomes difficult, and spirits stir.

name: Tomb Road
description: Opens a temporary passage or active threshold between the living world and the liminal realm of the dead.

name: Throne of the Last Silence
description: The supreme necromantic rite: the caster enthrones themselves as arbiter of the local boundary between life and death, commanding corpses, compelling spirits, and making mortality an immediate law of the scene.
